title: NUS-8-Confined CsPbBr3 Nanocrystals with Enhanced Photoluminescence and Ambient Stability through Ligand-Free Mechanosynthesis
abstract: CsPbBr 3 perovskite quantum dots (PQDs) are promising emitters for lighting and displays, but uncontrolled growth, surface defects, and environmental degradation limit their practical use. Herein, we report a multifunctional confined nanoreactor strategy that combines spatial confinement with interfacial defect regulation to simultaneously control the nucleation and photoluminescence stability of CsPbBr 3 PQDs. NUS-8, a two-dimensional Zr-based MOF with mesoporous channels and abundant carboxyl sites, serves as the host to confine PQD formation through chemical interactions. A ligand-free mechanochemical method is used to trigger the in-situ nucleation of CsPbBr 3 QDs within the nanospace of NUS-8, yielding uniformly confined nanocrystals of approximately 3–5 nm. The nanospace of NUS-8 regulates crystal growth by restricting particle migration, while coordination between carboxyl groups and Pb 2+ reconstructs the interfacial electronic environment and inhibits trap-assisted non-radiative recombination. The optimized CsPbBr 3 @NUS-8 composite exhibits a photoluminescence quantum yield of 55% and an average lifetime of 170.9 ns, demonstrating effective suppression of defect-mediated recombination. The CsPbBr 3 @NUS-8 composite retains ~ 85% of its initial PL intensity after 50 days of storage in air and ~ 72% after 168 h of continuous UV irradiation. In addition, the composite can be used for white LED fabrication and fluorescent patterning, demonstrating its potential for stable optoelectronic devices.

title: Electronic Structure of Co-Phthalocyanine Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) composed of metal phthalocyanines (MPc; MPc-MOF) are predicted to possess electronic structures similar to those of Dirac materials, such as the Lieb lattice and the fes lattice. Therefore, in this study, we first investigated the energy band structure of CoPc-MOF using density functional theory (DFT). According to previous theoretical studies, if the lattice structure of CoPc-MOF is regarded as a Lieb lattice, its π-band is predicted to exhibit stronger Dirac-band-like characteristics compared to other MPc-MOFs containing metals. The electron density obtained from the energy band calculations indicated that the contribution of the central metal to the π-band of CoPc-MOF is small; therefore, the lattice structure can be assumed to be more similar to the fes lattice than to the Lieb lattice. Next, we evaluated the crystal structure of the synthesized CoPc-MOF using X-ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The TEM images revealed that the synthesized CoPc-MOF powder consists of flake-like microcrystals, in which crystal growth along the molecular layer stacking direction is minimal. Furthermore, the absorption spectra in the visible and near-infrared (Vis–NIR) regions indicate that CoPc-MOF is a narrow-gap semiconductor with an optical gap of approximately 0.36 eV. On the other hand, DFT calculations indicate that the CoPc-MOF crystal is metallic due to the formation of a π-band in the interlayer direction (along the c-axis), which is inconsistent with the experimental results. This suggests that the synthesized CoPc-MOF may not be sufficiently stacked in the interlayer direction. This finding is consistent with the TEM images, which show that CoPc-MOF consists of flake-like microcrystalline structures. Energy band calculations were performed on a single monolayer of CoPc-MOF; however, even a single monolayer of CoPc-MOF behaves as a metal when electronic correlations are not explicitly considered, which contradicts the Vis–NIR and UPS experimental results. The single molecular layer of CoPc-MOF exhibited a metallic ground state because the π-d bands near the Fermi level formed the Fermi surface. In conclusion, the DFT+U energy-band calculations for the CoPc-MOF monolayer reproduced a semiconducting ground state and best explained the UPS spectra. These results indicate that the electronic correlation effects are significant in the 2D π-d bands near the Fermi level of a single molecular layer of CoPc-MOF.

title: Atomic‐Scale Origin of Charge Density Wave–Driven Metal–Semiconductor Transition in an Incommensurately Modulated Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: ABSTRACT Although metal–organic frameworks are widely recognized for their long‐range crystalline periodicity, they can also exhibit intrinsic aperiodic structures associated with incommensurate modulation, whose observation has been exceptionally rare. In low‐dimensional condensed matter physics, these unique structures often give rise to novel physical phenomena such as charge density wave. However, owing to limited direct experimental evidence, the relationship between incommensurate structural modulation and temperature‐dependent electronic transport in conductive metal–organic frameworks remains incompletely understood. Here, using high‐quality Pr 3 HHTP 2 (HHTP = 2,3,6,7,10,11‐hexahydroxytriphenylene) single crystals as a model system, we resolve the incommensurately modulated structure at 100 K (modulation vector q = 0.39143(12) c * ) via temperature‐dependent single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction. The observed reversible metal–semiconductor transition near 350 K occurs in a similar temperature range to the disappearance of the structural modulation, supporting a connection between lattice distortion and electronic behavior. The modulation reappears upon cooling, with guest water molecules influencing both the extent of its recovery and the electrical conductivity of the material. This work establishes a concrete experimental criterion for one‐dimensional charge density wave in metal‐organic frameworks and provides an ideal platform for probing coupled electronic–lattice modulations.

title: Encapsulating Metal–Organic Cluster in Metal–Organic Framework Film for Tandem Amplifying Third‐Order Nonlinear Optics
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) and metal–organic clusters (MOCs) are promising platforms for third‐order nonlinear optics (NLO) because their inorganic–organic components enable designable structures and tunable photo/electronic properties. However, integrating MOFs and MOCs for tandem third‐order NLO remains unexplored. Here, we combine MOF and MOC for third‐order NLO by encapsulating MOC in a porous MOF film. A [001]‐oriented conductive MOF Ni‐HHTP film (HHTP = 2,3,6,7,10,11‐hexahydroxytriphenylene) is prepared by liquid‐phase heating drop‐coating and shows excellent electro‐regulated third‐order NLO. Furthermore, iron‐based MOC (FeOC) is encapsulated into the ordered nanochannels of Ni‐HHTP film (Ni‐HHTP@FeOC) using an immersion strategy. The results show that the encapsulation of FeOC in the Ni‐HHTP film can enhance charge transfer and improve excited‐state absorption, with the nonlinear absorption coefficient ( β ) increasing from 4.9 × 10 −6 to 9.7 × 10 −6 m/W after loading. An applied electric field further modulates carrier concentration and excited‐state lifetime, enabling dynamic adjustment of the third‐order NLO response; β increased to 19.6 × 10 −6 m/W for Ni‐HHTP@FeOC‐2 V. This work is the first to combine MOF and MOC materials for high third‐order NLO performance and provides a synergistic strategy for regulating third‐order NLO performance through tandem encapsulation and electronic stimulation, offering new design concepts for adaptive optoelectronic devices.

title: Urchin-Like Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles Lower Intraocular Pressure through PARP1 Inhibition
abstract: Abstract Elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) drives glaucoma progression, yet durable control is limited by incomplete mechanistic targeting and inefficient anterior-segment drug delivery. Here, we identify poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase 1 (PARP1) hyperactivation as a redox-sensitive control node governing conventional outflow failure. In human trabecular meshwork and Schlemm’s canal tissues, upregulated PARP1, following oxidative stress, enforces nuclear retention of the ataxia telangiectasia mutated–NF-κB essential modulator (ATM–NEMO) complex. This suppresses cytoplasmic protein kinase B–endothelial nitric oxide synthase (AKT–eNOS) signaling and depletes intracellular nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+), effectively coupling DNA damage responses to nitric oxide deficiency and metabolic collapse. To reprogram this dual enzymatic–metabolic disturbance, we engineer a geometry-enhanced, pH-gated urchin-like mesoporous nanoplatform (hereafter denoted PUON@NMOF) that enables spatially segregated codelivery of the PARP1 inhibitor niraparib and the NAD+ precursor nicotinamide mononucleotide. The spiny nanoarchitecture enhances corneal adhesion and trans-epithelial transport, while the metal–organic framework (MOF) shell provides switchable release under mildly acidic microenvironments. Topical administration achieves preferential accumulation in outflow tissues, restores NAD+ pools, reactivates AKT–eNOS signaling and produces synergistic IOP reduction across distinct glaucoma models. These findings define the redox–PARP1 axis as a druggable vulnerability and establish materials-enabled dual-pathway correction as a strategy for precision modulation of outflow biomechanics.

title: Pathway-dependent chiral toroid self-assembly and topological transformations based on large π-conjugated dipeptides
abstract: Rational introduction of large π-conjugated moieties to peptides is crucial for their assembly, luminescence, chiral expression, and functional applications. In this work, a series of dipeptides functionalized with large conjugated benzoperylene imide segments are designed and synthesized, demonstrating programmable chiroptical and self-assembly behaviors. Water as poor solvent is identified as a critical factor governing the self-assembly of these dipeptides, by modulating the balance of intermolecular interactions to produce diverse morphologies such as nanoparticles, helical fibers, toroids and supercoiled structures. The assembly pathway progresses through multiple stages governed by diffusion-limited kinetics, interfacial energy minimization, and chiral internal stress. By varying the concentration, aging time, and temperature, it is possible to achieve diverse chiral morphological transitions, thereby enabling the preparation of toroids with both high phase purity and pronounced chiroptical activity. Furthermore, enantiomeric excess transforms toroids into helical rods, with racemic mixtures undergoing spontaneous resolution. Structural evolution and pronounced chiroptical activity, including strong circularly polarized luminescence, are confirmed by spectroscopic and diffraction analyses. This work offers new insights into both the mechanistic understanding of supramolecular chirality and an engineering framework for designing π conjugated dipeptide-based functional materials with tailored chiroptical properties. Rational introduction of large π-conjugated moieties to peptides is crucial for their assembly, luminescence, chiral expression, and functional applications. Here the authors functionalize a series of dipeptides with large conjugated benzoperylene imide segments demonstrating programmable chiroptical and self-assembly behaviors.

title: Prodrug-Based Self-Assembly Enables Dual-Triggered Release of Triazole Fungicide with Improved Environmental Safety
abstract: Abstract Stimuli-responsive prodrug-based controlled-release systems enable precise spatiotemporal regulation of the site-specific activation and release of active ingredients, thereby enhancing overall efficacy while minimizing off-target effects in pesticide application. In this study, cyproconazole (CPZ) was covalently conjugated with cinnamic acid (CAA) via a hydrolyzable ester bond to yield a prodrug (CCP), which spontaneously self-assembled into uniform nanoparticles (CCP NPs) without the addition of any auxiliary adjuvants. Benefiting from its small hydrodynamic diameter (277 nm), narrow size distribution (PDI = 0.139), and high surface charge (–33.2 mV), the resulting CCP NPs exhibited significantly improved foliar retention and spreading capacity on plant leaf surfaces. Compared with commercial CPZ suspension concentrate (CPZ SC), CCP NPs reduced soil leaching by 71.81% and 57.48% in yellowish-brown soil from Beijing and red soil from Yunnan Province, respectively. Furthermore, CCP NPs displayed pH- and esterase-dual-triggered release behavior and provided long-term antifungal activity against plant pathogens with a control efficacy of 74.86%, outperforming CPZ SC (50.36%) after 14 days of foliar application. Comprehensive biosafety evaluations revealed that CCP NPs had no adverse effects on plant growth and exhibited approximately 5-fold lower acute toxicity to earthworms. Overall, this CAA-based prodrug nano assembly provides an effective strategy that simultaneously enhances efficacy and curbs environmental mobility, thereby supporting the development of sustainable crop protection products.

title: Confinement Enables Direct Electrosynthesis of Acetaldoxime From CO and Nitrate
abstract: ABSTRACT Aldoximes are vital feedstocks in the fields of medicine, agriculture, and industry, yet their conventional synthesis suffers from high environmental costs and carbon footprints. Here, we report a direct electrocatalytic route to acetaldoxime via CO and NO 3 − co‐reduction. The C–N coupling efficiency in this process hinges on the kinetic match between CO reduction and NO 3 − reduction. Acetaldoxime synthesis exemplifies this challenge: sluggish C–C dimerization contrasts with rapid NO 3 − RR, leading to over‐reduction of nitrogen species to NH 3 . We hypothesized that a confinement strategy could selectively promote C–C dimerization and enrich acetaldehyde intermediate, thereby facilitating oximation. Ultrasmall Cu nanoparticles were encapsulated within SBA‐15 mesopores to selectively accelerate the dimerization step. Combined operando Raman and in situ differential electrochemical mass spectrometry reveal that the confined Cu lowers the overpotential for the key C 2 intermediate to align with that for NH 2 OH generation, enabling efficient C–N coupling to acetaldoxime. The optimized Cu@SBA‐15 catalyst achieves an acetaldoxime production rate of 255.1 mmol g cat. − 1 h − 1 (partial current density: 24.6 mA cm − 2 ). This work establishes a sustainable pathway toward aldoximes, aligning with green chemistry principles while expanding the toolbox for electrocatalytic C–N bond formation.

title: Cryptochiral Circularly Polarized Luminescence Emerges From Cosolvent‐Regulated Pathway Complexity in Amyloidogenic Peptide Self‐Assembly
abstract: ABSTRACT Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) is important for chiral photonics, optical encryption, bioimaging, and information processing. It is usually associated with an identifiable chiral ground‐state organization, and CPL without detectable ground‐state chirality remains comparatively unexplored. Herein, we report a rare “ cryptochiral CPL ” phenomenon arising from cosolvent‐regulated pathway complexity in the self‐assembly of a naphthalimide (NMI)‐amyloidogenic peptide conjugate (PEP‐L). In water, PEP‐L spontaneously forms thermodynamically stable, emissive nanofibers with pronounced supramolecular chirality and strong CPL. Adding a small amount of cosolvent redirects assembly toward kinetically trapped spherical nanoassemblies and shows no detectable Circular Dichroism (CD) response in the naphthalimide chromophore region, but retains pronounced CPL, which decouples ground‐state and excited‐state chiroptical responses. We term this behavior cryptochiral CPL . Thermal annealing or aging converts the spheres into thermodynamically favored nanofibers with distinct CD and CPL characteristics. The enantiomer PEP‐D shows mirror‐image chiroptical responses, which validates the phenomenon. Density functional theory (DFT) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations under different conditions give molecular‐level insight into the conformation, noncovalent interactions, and supramolecular organization of the different assembly states. These findings establish a new conceptual framework for adaptive chiral photonic materials and open opportunities for hidden optical encoding and biomolecular photonic systems.

title: Ligand Curvature Controls the Size of Self-Assembled Twisted Metallacycles
abstract: Abstract Coordination-driven self-assembly often yields dynamic libraries of metallacycles whose size distribution is difficult to control, and ligand-design strategies for directing such equilibria have so far been limited to discrete changes in coordination angles. Here we introduce the first twisted metallacycles, in which ligand curvature is tuned through the tether-to-twist approach. Two twistacene dipyridyl ligands with only a 6° difference in the overall bend: the nearly planar Pl (14° twist) and the twisted Tw (34° twist) assemble with (dppp)Pd(II) and (dppp)Pt(II) corners {M} into dynamic equilibria between rhomboidal {M}2L2 and hexagonal {M}3L3 metallacycles. NMR, nanoESI-MS and X-ray crystallography show that racemic ligands self-sort with high fidelity: socially, into heterochiral meso {M}2L2 rhomboids, and narcissistically, into homochiral {M}3L3 hexagons. Van ‘t Hoff analysis shows ring expansion to be endothermic and entropy-driven throughout, with an enthalpic cost rising from 6–10 kJ mol–1 for Pl to 17–18 kJ mol–1 for Tw. This is explained by increased strain energy for mismatched planar ligands in {M}2L2 assemblies. A few degrees of backbone curvature therefore reshape the free-energy landscape of coordination-driven self-assembly.

title: Water-Soluble Pd12 Multicomponent Cage Enables Selective Separation of 1,4-Dibromonaphthalene from 1,5-Dibromonaphthalene and Regioselective Bromination of Naphthalene
abstract: Abstract The synthesis of intricate supramolecular architectures is driven by the desire to translate structural complexity into functional specificity. Herein, we report the formation of an unusual M12L4L′4 cage (MCC) with double-walled knotted architecture via multicomponent self-assembly of a tripyridyl ligand (L), a tricarboxylate ligand (L′), and a cis-Pd(II) acceptor (M). The structure of the MCC resembles a truncated tetrahedron with two overlaid walls enclosing a distorted cavity. The cavity selectively encapsulates polyaromatic hydrocarbons with two fused rings like naphthalene (G1) and its derivatives [1,4-dibromonaphthalene (G5) and 1,5-dibromonaphthalene (G6)], while it is repellent to larger guests in aqueous media. Interestingly, it shows high selectivity for 1,4-dibromonaphthalene (G5), which enabled the purification of 1,4-dibromonaphthalene and 1,5-dibromonaphthalene (G6) from their mixture in aqueous media. Furthermore, selective bromination of naphthalene to 1,4-dibromonaphthalene could be achieved within the hydrophobic cavity of MCC in aqueous media under ambient reaction conditions driven by the high specificity of the cavity for G5, while the same bromination in the absence of the cage yields a mixture of dibromo and monobromo derivatives. Thus, the newly designed cage (MCC) could be utilized for developing an efficient strategy for the regioselective bromination of naphthalene, overcoming the challenges associated with separating the product mixture generated in conventional bromination. Moreover, the cage enables efficient separation of the dibromo isomers of naphthalene formed in conventional synthesis.

title: In Situ STEM Imaging of Colloidal Crystals Based on Programmable Atom Equivalents
abstract: Abstract It is challenging to image the assembly of colloidal crystals composed of programmable atom equivalents (PAEs) using electron microscopy (EM). PAEs typically consist of nanoparticle cores densely functionalized with radially oriented DNA shells, which assemble in the liquid phase via DNA bonds. EM requires high-vacuum conditions, and electron beams can damage soft materials like nucleic acids. Here, we present a liquid-phase scanning transmission electron microscopy (LPSTEM) method for imaging PAEs composed of ∼5 nm gold nanoparticle cores in solution, enabling the direct investigation of their DNA-directed assembly processes. This system is particularly well-suited for in situ studies of soft-matter dynamics because the gold nanoparticle cores provide strong electron contrast. Using a nanofluidic liquid cell, the nucleation and growth of PAE assemblies, governed via the principles of colloidal crystal engineering with DNA, were directly observed. Imaging conditions were established to resolve colloidal assemblies in liquid while also characterizing electron-beam-induced damage under both conventional STEM and STEM-in-SEM conditions. Quantitative image analysis reveals changes in local coordination during crystal growth and subsequent beam-induced dissociation. Complementary ex situ simulations corroborate that radiolytic species generated in the buffer are major contributors to beam-induced damage. Together, these results establish a versatile and accessible platform for probing the in situ dynamics of PAE assembly in liquids, with broad applicability to the study of other soft nanomaterials and composites relevant to sensing, actuation, energy storage, catalysis, and medicine.

title: Atomic Bridges Directionally Assemble Nanoclusters into Conductive Nanowires for Enhanced CO2 Electroreduction
abstract: Abstract One-dimensional (1D) nanowires, owing to their directional charge transport properties, represent an excellent catalytic platform for overcoming electron and proton transport bottlenecks in electrocatalysis. In this work, we directionally assemble discrete Cu6 nanoclusters into Cu6 nanowires (Cu6-NWs) using an atomically designed “atomic bridge”, achieving long-range order at the atomic scale. The resulting Cu6-NWs exhibit an electrical conductivity of 8.2 × 10–4 S·cm–1, which is 8 orders of magnitude higher than that of discrete Cu6 nanoclusters, highlighting the superiority of the wire-like ordered structure in charge transport. In the CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR), Cu6-NWs achieve a Faraday efficiency (FE) of 64.8% for hydrocarbon products (CH4 and C2H4) at −1.1 V, reversing the hydrogen evolution-dominated catalytic behavior observed for isolated Cu6 nanoclusters. Mechanistic studies reveal that the linear configuration of Cu6-NWs strengthens the coupling between electron and proton transport. Moreover, it modulates the d-band center via active-site migration, thereby tuning the activity and selectivity of CO2RR. The atomic-bridge-directed assembly strategy offers a perspective for designing high-performance catalysts.

title: One‐Step Conversion of Thermoplastic Elastomers into Ionic Ordered Mesoporous Polymers via Interface‐Directed Chain Scission: A Plastic Upcycling Strategy for Atmospheric Water Harvesting
abstract: ABSTRACT As a cornerstone of the circular materials economy, chemical recycling typically breaks commodity plastics down into small molecular building blocks. While this strategy is reasonable for most plastics, styrenic thermoplastic elastomers (TPEs) can be a notable exception. These materials can intrinsically self‐assemble into ordered nanostructures, yet most upcycling methods discard this morphological asset, leaving TPEs a compelling but underexploited feedstock for high‐value applications. Here, we report a one‐step approach that upcycles TPEs into ionic ordered mesoporous polymers (OMPs) in their solid state, through interface‐directed chain scission. Adding a small amount of radical initiator (dicumyl peroxide) during the sulfonation of polystyrene‐ block ‐poly(ethylene‐ran‐butylene)‐ block ‐polystyrene (SEBS) leverages a diffusion‐controlled reaction front to selectively cleave the minority polystyrene domains, while crosslinking and sulfonating the majority phase. This one‐step process at 145°C installs ionic character and establishing uniform mesoporosity without the high‐temperature calcination (typically > 350°C) that conventionally erodes functional groups. Furthermore, the resulting OMPs act as high‐performance sorbents for atmospheric water harvesting, demonstrating rapid kinetics, solar‐driven regeneration, and excellent cycling stability, while a simple lithium chloride (LiCl) encapsulation step enhances their water uptake capacity to 2.46 g/g.

title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
abstract: Although inverted perovskite solar cells now deliver certified efficiencies approaching their single-junction limits, their practical deployment remains constrained by the thermo-mechanical fragility of buried interfaces under realistic temperature fluctuations. Here, we identify thermo-mechanically driven, stress-accumulation-dominated adhesion failure at self-assembled monolayer-based buried interfaces as a critical failure mode in inverted perovskite solar cells. To address this issue, we propose an interfacial robustness design strategy based on a homometallic halide pretreatment, which constructs a chemically compatible and highly anchorable interfacial environment on transparent conductive oxides to guide the ordered assembly of SAMs. This interfacial treatment increases the density of surface hydroxyl species and enables hierarchical multipoint interfacial anchoring dominated by metal-oxygen coordination, with Cl − induced hydrogen-bonding interactions acting cooperatively, thereby enhancing anchoring robustness and improving tolerance to thermo-mechanical stress accumulation. With this interfacial strategy, the devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 27.3% (26.9% certified) and retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between −40 and 85°C (ISOS-T-3). These results demonstrate that rational regulation of buried interfacial anchoring architectures can simultaneously enhance device efficiency and long-term operational reliability, offering a viable pathway toward high-efficiency and durable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Amine Vapor Activated Superior Proton Conduction in a Barium Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) show promise as solid electrolytes for proton exchange membrane fuel cells, yet progress is hindered by a limited number of proton-conductive materials and an incomplete understanding of the underlying mechanisms. This study presents a 3D barium-based MOF, {[Ba(p-CPhH2IDC)(H2O)2]}n (Ba-MOF-1), synthesized using 2-(4-carboxyphenyl)-1H-imidazole-4,5-dicarboxylic acid. Its structure features abundant unprotonated carboxyl oxygens, imidazole nitrogens, and coordinated water, creating a favorable environment for proton transport. While Ba-MOF-1 exhibits modest proton conductivity under humid conditions (1.13 × 10–5 S·cm–1 at 98% RH and 100 °C), its performance is dramatically enhanced upon exposure to volatile bases. At 100 °C in 2 M ammonia vapor, conductivity surges to 5.26 × 10–3 S·cm–1-a 465-fold increase. Similarly, at 70 °C, vapors from 2 M methylamine, dimethylamine, and ethylamine solutions boost conductivity by factors of 367, 299, and 230, respectively, compared to humid conditions alone. This enhancement is attributed to the adsorption of basic molecules within the MOF’s pores, where they act both as additional proton carriers and as direct proton sources, synergistically facilitating proton conduction.

title: A Cryptic Cytochrome P450 Radical Cyclase Catalyzes Naphthalene-Ring Closure in Rifamycin Biosynthesis
abstract: Abstract The enzymatic assembly of the 8-hydroxynaphthalene chromophore in rifamycins presents a classic biosynthetic paradox: the off-PKS precursor, prorifamycin A (1a), readily suffers nonenzymatic deoxygenative collapse in solution into the aberrant product 8-deoxynaphthoquinones. Here, using in cellulo genetic manipulation, stepwise pathway reconstitution, in vitro enzymatic assays, molecular docking, and DFT calculations, we identified Rif-Orf0 to be a cytochrome P450 radical cyclase. Rif-Orf0 converted 1a to the 8-hydroxy-7,8-dihydronaphthalenoid intermediate prorifamycin B (1b) through a low-barrier biradical cyclization, and the RifS/RifT dehydrogenase pair rapidly captured and oxidatively aromatized 1b to 34a-deoxyrifamycin W (2). This Rif-Orf0 and RifS/RifT enzymatic cascade outcompeted the spontaneous deoxygenative shunting that afforded 8-deoxynaphthalene-type rifamycins, thereby enforcing the production of 8-hydroxynaphthalenoid rifamycins. This study expanded the catalytic repertoire of cytochrome P450 enzymes and resolved a long-standing question in rifamycin biosynthesis by characterizing how tailoring enzymes canalized reactive intermediates from spontaneous reactions toward defined natural product architectures.

title: Synergistic Lewis Base Organocatalysis and Electrocatalysis for the Enantioselective Construction of α‐Fluorinated Quaternary Stereocenters
abstract: ABSTRACT The construction of α‐fluorinated quaternary stereocenters—a structural motif of high value in pharmaceuticals and bioactive molecules—remains a formidable synthetic challenge due to inherent steric and stereoelectronic constraints. Herein, we report a synergistic strategy combining chiral isothiourea (ITU) organocatalysis with electrochemistry, enabling the direct and highly enantioselective α‐alkylation of bench‐stable fluorinated acetic esters with both silyl enol ethers and allylsilanes. This approach integrates anodic single‐electron oxidation with asymmetric Lewis base catalysis, converting in situ‐generated disubstituted C1‐ammonium enolates into configurationally well‐defined, chiral ITU‐bound α‐carbonyl tertiary radical intermediates. Subsequent stereocontrolled radical cross‐coupling with SOMOphilic partners furnishes a broad range of esters bearing α‐fluorinated quaternary stereocenters in high yields (up to 95%) and excellent enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee). This work not only fills a significant gap in the single‐electron chemistry of disubstituted C1‐ammonium enolates but also provides a versatile platform for the rapid assembly of optically active α‐fluorinated quaternary carbonyl compounds, with significant potential in drug discovery and complex molecule synthesis.

title: Bidirectional Sulfur Redox Regulation Enabling Ultra‐Stable High‐Sulfur‐Loading All‐Solid‐State Lithium‐Sulfur Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state lithium‐sulfur batteries are promising for high‐energy storage but are limited by sluggish sulfur redox and poor cycling stability. Herein, we design a new amorphous‐crystalline Li 6.05 P 0.95 Nb 0.05 S 5 Cl 0.8 I 0.2 electrolyte that reconstructs interfacial Li + transport and enables bidirectional regulation of sulfur redox. The amorphous structure improves solid‐solid contact and creates additional continuous Li + pathways around sulfur, while the crystal framework maintains fast Li + ion‐conducting channels. During the discharge, we further uncover an Nb reduction mechanism in which Nb 4+ is reduced to Nb 3+ , generating Li‐rich sites that promote Li 2 S nucleation and sulfur reduction. During the charge, I − is oxidized to I 2 , which acts as the redox mediator for Li 2 S oxidation, while I 3 − formation helps stabilize unconsumed I 2 . This bidirectional regulation enables 84.2% sulfur utilization at a high sulfur loading of 6 mg cm − 2 and retains 736 mAh g − 1 with 93.1% capacity retention after 1500 cycles at 0.5 C. These findings provide a mechanistic strategy for high‐sulfur‐loading all‐solid‐state Li‐S batteries.

title: Hydroxamate Reticular Chemistry beyond Metals: Single-Crystalline Two- and Three-Dimensional Boron–Hydroxamate Covalent Organic Frameworks
abstract: Abstract Hydroxamate chelation has already enabled robust metal–organic frameworks. Here, to move the corresponding reticular chemistry beyond metal nodes, hydroxamate chelation has been integrated within heteroleptic tetracoordinate B(O,O)(N)(C) centers to construct four single-crystalline boron–hydroxamate covalent organic frameworks, namely SUM-306–SUM-309. Bayesian optimization enabled the growth of diffraction-quality SUM-306 single crystals, while linker isomerism and functionalization yielded a series spanning two-dimensional hcb and three-dimensional pcu-h frameworks. Structural comparison reveals extended anti-B–phenylene–B arrangements in SUM-306 and SUM-307 and folded syn arrangements in SUM-308 and SUM-309, associated with their respective two- and three-dimensional propagation. Solid-state NMR spectroscopy, B K-edge XANES, and electronic-structure calculations support tetracoordinate boron formation and differentiated yet substantial bonding throughout the B(O,O)(N)(C) environment. As a representative of the series, SUM-308 retains accessible microporosity, exhibits a BET surface area of 1279.9 m2 g–1, and preferentially adsorbs and dynamically separates CO2 from N2. These results extend hydroxamate reticular chemistry beyond metals and establish a mixed-linkage strategy combining chelation, donor–acceptor coordination, and covalent anchoring for single-crystalline boron-based framework construction.

title: [8+4]‐Connected Ether‐Oxygen‐Based 3D COF Redox Mediators for Durable Light‐Assisted Indirect Electrocatalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Ether‐oxygen is a type of functional group with high chemical stability, electronic modulation capability, and imparted molecular flexibility, yet incorporating ether‐oxygen groups into high‐connectivity covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to explore their extended applications remains a challenge. Herein, we have designed a series of [8+4]‐connected 3D COFs with scu topology, named TADM–TAPP–COF(M) (M = Ni, Mn, and Cu), by introducing eight‐connected ether‐oxygen based building blocks and metalloporphyrin nodes, which can be applied in high‐stability light‐assisted indirect electrocatalysis. These 3D COFs exhibit good crystallinity, nanosheet morphology, flexible 3D pore structure, abundant ether‐oxygen groups and active metal sites, and excellent electrolyte affinity, which can act as efficient redox mediators. Impressively, the Ni‐incorporated structure TADM–TAPP–COF (Ni) demonstrates high yield in the condensation cyclization reaction of aromatic aldehydes and 2‐aminobenzenethiol to produce 2‐phenylbenzothiazole (yields up to 96%), coupled with the simultaneous production of gas‐phase H 2 product (∼1.15 mmol g −1 h −1 ). Notably, it also shows remarkable stability (continuous reaction for 300 h), high recyclability (8 cycles), and scale‐up production ability (about 2 g in a 12 h batch experiment) and wide substrate applicability, providing a valuable example for the structural design of catalysts toward light‐assisted indirect electrocatalysis.

title: Calcium–porphyrin metal organic framework/starch hybrid beads for pH-responsive and photostable drug delivery of Nifuroxazide and Omeprazole
abstract: Drug-loaded beads have attracted significant interest as advanced delivery systems due to their ability to enhance drug stability, bioavailability, and controlled release. Omeprazole and Nifuroxazide suffer from challenges such as acid degradation, poor dissolution, and limited stability, which can reduce their therapeutic effectiveness. Encapsulation within bead-based carriers protects these drugs from gastrointestinal conditions and enables targeted release, thereby improving their overall therapeutic performance. To overcome these drawbacks, this work has engineered a novel oral drug delivery system in the form of a Ca-TCPP/starch bead. This innovative platform leverages the porous structure of the Ca-TCPP material to achieve substantial drug encapsulation and high loading capabilities. In this study, a calcium-tetrakis(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin (Ca-TCPP) MOF was successfully synthesized and incorporated into starch-based spherical beads to construct a hybrid inorganic-organic carrier with improved structural stability and controlled release behaviour. Comprehensive characterization using FT-IR, PXRD, SEM, EDX, and BET analyses confirmed the formation of a mesoporous composite featuring uniformly dispersed nanocrystalline MOF domains within the biopolymeric matrix. The Ca-TCPP@starch beads were evaluated as drug delivery vehicles for Nifuroxazide and omeprazole. Both drugs exhibit stability limitations under physiological conditions. The system demonstrated high encapsulation efficiencies across different concentrations (90% for Nifuroxazide and 85% for omeprazole). Kinetic modelling of Nifuroxazide indicated that a zero-order model predominantly governs the release profile, while for omeprazole, the first-order kinetic model yielded the best fit for all formulations. Additionally, photostability investigations showed that the hybrid matrix significantly retards light-induced degradation, particularly for Nifuroxazide, while preserving the pH-dependent stability of omeprazole. Overall, the developed composite integrates high surface area, tunable porosity, and environmental responsiveness within a single platform. These findings highlight the potential of Ca-TCPP MOF-starch hybrids as a versatile system for drug delivery applications demanding controlled release and enhanced chemical protection.

title: Covalent Organic Framework‐Templated Spatial Confinement of Self‐Assembled Monolayers for High‐Performance Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) have emerged as efficient hole‐contacting layers for p‐i‐n perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, incomplete SAM coverage and weak bonding with the substrate result in heterogeneous buried interfaces. Herein, a covalent organic framework (COF)‐templated spatial confinement (CTSC) strategy is developed by employing a newly designed phosphonate–carbazole‐based COF, namely COF‐TPACz , to regulate the buried interface. The nanoscale island‐like COF domains could restrict the penetration of aggregated SAM molecules and allow well‐distributed ones to anchor on exposed substrates. Meanwhile, hydrogen‐bonding and π–π interactions between COF‐TPACz and SAM favor a more uniform molecular arrangement on the COF domains. These adjustments synergistically suppress molecular aggregation and improve surface coverage, yielding a denser and more homogeneous SAM interface. Furthermore, the improved interface optimizes upper perovskite crystallization, promotes compact and vertically extended grains, and strengthens buried interfacial contact, thereby suppressing nonradiative recombination and facilitating charge extraction and transport. Consequently, the CTSC‐based PSCs achieve a peak efficiency of 27.03%, together with enhanced long‐term stability. We believe these findings provide a conceptual advance for realizing homogeneous SAM via spatial confinement and a viable route toward efficient and stable PSCs.

title: Electronic Polarization in Covalent Organic Frameworks With Alternating Hetero‐Linkages for High‐Performance H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) hold considerable promise for photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production, yet achieving efficient carrier separation and transport to achieve excellent performance remains a significantly challenge. Herein, we constructed a library of polarized COFs featuring alternating hetero‐linkage C═N and C─N linkages, which establish continuous local charge gradients at molecular level. Remarkably, driven by the localized electronic polarization microenvironment, the optimal material (TPPZ‐BC) showed a photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production rate as high as 11.06 mmol g −1 h −1 , outperforming most reported COF‐based photocatalysts. Mechanistic studies revealed that the spatial alternation of electron‐withdrawing C═N and electron‐donating C─N linkages induced a strong intramolecular charge polarization. This effect significantly modulates the surface electrostatic potential distribution, increasing the proportion of highly positive regions and thereby enhancing the adsorption and activation of oxygen molecules. Moreover, this structural design breaks molecular symmetry and promotes the synergistic alignment of local dipoles, generating a robust intrinsic electric field. This work provides a new strategy for the development of crystalline porous photocatalysts toward highly efficient photosynthesis.

title: Radical Molecular-Junction Covalent Organic Framework for Asymmetric Iodide Conversion: 100,000 Cycles in Zn-Iodine Batteries
abstract: Abstract Aqueous Zinc–iodine batteries are promising for large-scale energy storage owing to their eco-friendliness and safety. However, conventional two-electron cathode hosts suffer from poor cycling life due to polyiodide shuttling and sluggish one-step I–/I2 redox kinetics, which limits their practical usage. Herein, we designed a molecular-junction covalent organic framework (COF) denoted as TNCOF, integrating the tetrathiafulvalene (TTF) donor and the naphthalene diimide (NDI) acceptor. Typically, TTF forms a robust radical-cationic TTF•+ structure by anchoring to iodine electrostatically. TTF•+ and electron-withdrawing NDI within the T•+NCOF molecular junction provide a driving force through an intense local electrostatic potential for the asymmetric iodine conversion (AIC) pathway (I–/I3–/I2 vs. I2/I–), markedly boosting reaction kinetics and suppressing polyiodide shuttling. The optimized T•+NCOF cathode delivers a specific capacity of 228.7 mAh g–1 at 1 A g–1 and achieves an ultralong cycling stability exceeding 100,000 cycles, which is one of the highest records in this field. In situ measurements, Peak Force Tunneling atomic force microscopy (AFM) results, and calculations confirm the robust adsorption capability of T•+NCOF and demonstrate the accelerated I3– conversion kinetics. This work establishes that a radical-cationic molecular-junction COF enables robust I3– anchoring and a unique AIC pathway, offering a novel strategy to overcome inherent stability challenges in Zinc-halogen batteries.

title: Taming Metal–Electrolyte Interface via Two-Dimensional Organic Metal Chalcogenide Colloids for Anode-Free Sodium Metal Batteries
abstract: Abstract Anode-free metal batteries are promising candidates for next-generation energy storage technologies, yet their application is severely limited by dendrite growth and rapid capacity decay induced by an unstable metal–electrolyte interface. Herein, we propose a “colloid electrolyte” strategy employing coordination polymer nanosheets as electrolyte additives for constructing anode-free sodium metal batteries (AFSMBs). Unlike conventional molecular additives or inert particle suspensions, these colloidal nanosheets provide spatially organized and continuously available interfacial reaction domains, thereby spatially regulating electrolyte component distribution and interfacial reactions. These nanosheets, composed of AgS layers uniformly decorated with fluorinated groups, undergo in situ decomposition at the metal–electrolyte interface. This process generates gradient distributions of Ag nanoparticles and NaF/Na2S species, which guide the spontaneous formation of a functionally graded solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). This hierarchical SEI enables dendrite-free Na deposition and imparts sustained interfacial protection during cycling. Consequently, high-cathode-loading AFSMBs achieve an ultralong lifespan (&gt;1600 cycles), representing a 10-fold improvement over counterpart cells without the colloidal additive. Notably, 0.5-Ah-level anode-free pouch cells exhibit stable cycling for 500 cycles at 2 C. This work establishes coordination polymer colloids as a new class of electrolyte additives for advanced alkali metal batteries.

title: Constructing Dynamic Interfacial Hydration Network Channel for Efficient Co‑Transport of OH − and H 2 in Water‑Electrolysis Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient mass transport at the electrode–electrolyte interface of anion‐exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEM‐WE) is fundamentally constrained by antagonistic hydration requirements. Drawing inspiration from biological channels that mediate hydrophilic yet non‐retentive transport, we designed a series of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with tunable sulfone densities as synthetic nanochannels. Combined experimental and theoretical investigations revealed that the sulfone moiety (O═S═O) established weak, labile hydrogen bonds with water, engendering a highly dynamic hydrogen‐bonding network. This unique hydration environment established a surface‐wetting yet bulk‐open state within the COF nanochannels, wherein a dynamic interfacial hydration network channel was maintained within the pores for efficient OH − conduction, while the bulk pore volume remained non‐flooded for unobstructed H 2 evacuation. When incorporated into the cathode catalyst layer, the sulfone‐rich 2S‐COF delivers a current density of 10.30 A cm −2 at 2.0 V under industrially relevant conditions (1 M KOH, 80°C), representing a 48% enhancement over the COF‐free electrode. This work establishes a bio‐inspired strategy for molecular‐level control of interfacial hydration, providing a generalizable platform for designing high‐performance electrochemical interfaces that require concurrent ion and gas management.

title: DNA‐Based Solar Cells: From Supramolecular Engineering to Photovoltaic Devices
abstract: Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), beyond its classical role as the molecule encoding genetic information, is gaining attention as a sustainable and multifunctional material for optoelectronic applications, including photovoltaic technologies. Its distinctive properties, e.g., thermal stability, water solubility, and programmable self‐assembly, offer unique opportunities for interface engineering and environmentally friendly processing. This review explores the structural and chemical features that make DNA suitable for optoelectronic applications and examines its integration into various solar cell architectures, including silicon, perovskite, organic, and dye‐sensitized systems. Emphasis is placed on its role in improving charge transport, stabilizing interfaces, and organizing chromophores. Emerging directions such as hierarchical nanostructures, biomimetic designs inspired by DNA’s helical geometry, and multifunctional scaffolds for complex nanocomposites are discussed as strategies to overcome current limitations. These advances position DNA as a nanoscale architect for next‐generation bio‐hybrid photovoltaics, paving the way for devices that combine efficiency, sustainability, and durability.

title: Surface-Driven Assembly of Bent-Core Liquid Crystals on HOPG: Insights into Kinetic and Thermodynamic Control from STM and Quantum Mechanical Simulations
abstract: The self-assembly of bent-core liquid crystals (BCLC) is critical for understanding and controlling interfacial ordering in functional soft materials. Here, we investigate the adsorption and 2D self-assembly of an azobenzene-containing BCLC molecule, AzB-BC, at the 1,2,4-trichlorobenzene/highly ordered pyrolytic graphite (HOPG(0001)) interface using scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations. STM imaging reveals the spontaneous formation of extended lamellar monolayers characterized by bright aromatic bands separated by head-to-head alkyl chains, with the emergence of multiple chiral domains at room temperature. Ex situ thermal annealing leads to a single-domain monolayer, indicating a transition from kinetically trapped assemblies to a thermodynamically favored configuration. STM image-guided periodic DFT calculations identify two low energy molecular conformations differing in the orientation of the terminal alkoxy chains, with similar adsorption energies on HOPG. The calculations show that π–π interactions between the aromatic bent-core units and the HOPG surface drive the surface orientation of the BCLC molecule, while alkyl chains primarily govern lateral packing through van der Waals interactions. Together, the combined experimental and theoretical results provide the first detailed insight into the adsorption energetics and conformational preferences of a bent-core liquid crystal on an ordered graphitic surface, offering a molecular-level framework for designing surface-confined liquid crystal systems.

title: Multilevel Asymmetric Janus Nanofabric with Universal Adhesion and Robust Reliability for Preventive Protection of Cultural Heritage
abstract: Cultural relics, as unique and non‐renewable historical treasures, demand conservation materials that reconcile the conflicting requirements, including universal adhesion, microenvironment regulation, long‐term reliability, and intelligent protection, while the microstructural heterogeneity essential for multifunctionality conflicts fundamentally with the topological homogeneity required for reliability. Here, we report a Janus fibrous membrane with multilevel asymmetrical and interface engineered, which spatially decouples mutually exclusive functionalities within integrated domains. Specifically, F m Si n PU resin incorporated dangling fluorinated chains that imparted hydrophobicity and low surface energy, while its polyurethane segmented backbone retained sufficient conformational symmetry to enable chain entanglement and mechanical cohesion, while P x PU resin integrated phosphorus‐containing flame‐retardant segments with abundant multi‐hydrogen bonds that promoted self‐assembly. Furthermore, coordinated interfacial interactions spanning three hierarchical contact regions enabled accurate regulation over porous architecture, surface chemical states, and dielectric microenvironment. Accordingly, the JFM@CD 10wt.% exhibited universal adhesion capability on various cultural relic substrates with binding energies ranging from −90.69 to −153.08 kcal/mol, hydrostatic pressure resistance of 58.3 kPa, air permeability of 167.9 mm/s, ultraviolet transmittance of 1.21%, and triboelectric output of 13.71 mW/m 2 for self‐powered autonomous alarming. The environmental verification confirmed significant, reliable protection across diverse cultural relic substrates. Remarkably, this work establishes a transformative paradigm for next‐generation intelligent cultural relic conservation materials.

title: Self-assembly of bacterial volumetric patterns directed by a synthetic reaction-diffusion circuit
abstract: Reaction-diffusion (RD) has long been proposed as a mechanism underlying biological pattern formation. However, quantitative frameworks linking circuit design to spatial organization remain limited. Here, we engineered a synthetic gene circuit, MINPAC, that couples gene expression regulation (reaction) with bacterial colony expansion and quorum sensing (diffusion) to guide bacterial cells to self-organize into periodic volumetric patterns across multiple scales, from single cells to three-dimensional colonies. The patterns exhibit robustness against environmental variations and size-dependent complexity. Mathematical modeling supports a clock-and-wavefront mechanism, where oscillatory gene expression interacts with outward expanding diffusions to generate these periodic spatial structures. Topological analysis reveals that specific network architecture is essential for pattern formation. Guided by model predictions, we further show that pattern complexity can be systematically tuned by gene dosage, with lower expression levels favoring multiple rings through faster dynamics. This work establishes a framework uniting circuit engineering and mathematical analysis for programming multicellular self-organization through RD mechanisms, with potential applications in regenerative medicine and biomaterials.

title: Membrane-confined self-assembly enables localized bioorthogonal prodrug activation and selective cancer therapy
abstract: Bioorthogonal prodrug activation offers a promising approach for site-specific drug release, significantly reducing the systemic toxicity associated with conventional chemotherapy. However, challenges remain in precisely controlling prodrug activation at the target site while maintaining optimal selectivity, reactivity, and potency. Here, we report a dual-targeting peptide, TzFFY p HH, that integrates on-membrane enzyme-instructed self-assembly (EISA) with bioorthogonal chemistry to enable selective chemotherapy. Exploiting the overexpression of alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) on cancer cells, TzFFY p HH selectively anchors and self-assembles on the cancer cell membrane, enriching tetrazine (Tz) handles that act as bioorthogonal reactors to activate a trans -cyclooctene (TCO)-caged prodrug (TCO-Dox) for precise drug release. Upon topical administration, TzFFY p HH forms a hydrogel at subcutaneous tumor sites, enabling in situ prodrug activation for effective tumor inhibition. Notably, this localized chemotherapy elicits a potent antitumor immune response, which, when combined with anti-programmed death-1 antibody (αPD-1), synergistically potentiates therapeutic outcomes. By coupling supramolecular self-assembly with bioorthogonal reactivity on the cell membrane, this work establishes a chemically programmable platform for spatiotemporally controlled prodrug activation and provides a general strategy for integrating localized chemotherapy with immunotherapy.

title: Proximity-Triggered DNA Self-Assembly for Selective Regulation of Membrane Receptors on Living Cells
abstract: Abstract Membrane receptors activate downstream signaling through oligomerization to regulate cellular behaviors, yet selectively modulating membrane receptor signaling in cancer cells remains challenging. Here, we report a proximity-triggered DNA self-assembly (PTDSA) strategy for cancer-cell-selective receptor regulation. PTDSA uses aptamers targeting the cancer-cell biomarker EpCAM and receptor c-Met as proximity triggers. Only when EpCAM and c-Met are simultaneously bound and spatially proximal does toehold-mediated strand displacement initiate catalytic hairpin assembly, generating a proximity-triggered hybrid intermediate. Through programmable DNA sequences, this intermediate recruits probe-bound lysosomal shuttling receptors (IGFIIR) to form functional PTDSA complexes. These complexes hijack lysosomal trafficking pathways to deliver c-Met for degradation, thereby suppressing downstream oncogenic signaling. In HeLa cells, PTDSA achieved 35% c-Met degradation and inhibited cell migration by 33%. This work establishes PTDSA as a DNA-programmable platform for cancer-cell-selective membrane receptor degradation and modulation, offering a strategy to overcome the nonspecificity of conventional receptor-targeting approaches.

title: Molecularly Programmed Piezoelectric Peptide Interfaces Couple Energy Conversion with Cell Recognition for Neural Regeneration
abstract: Electrical regulation of tissue regeneration occurs at dynamic biointerfaces, where cells integrate mechanical, biochemical, and electrical cues from their surrounding microenvironment. Engineering biodegradable materials that simultaneously establish bioactive interfaces and convert externally applied mechanical energy into localized bioelectrical signals remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we establish a molecular programming strategy for constructing bioactive piezoelectric biointerfaces through sequence-defined peptide self-assembly. Guided by multiscale molecular simulations, an amphiphilic peptide hierarchically assembles into noncentrosymmetric two-dimensional nanopatches in which electromechanical energy conversion, cell recognition, and intrinsic antioxidant activity emerge cooperatively from a single supramolecular architecture. Upon clinically compatible ultrasound stimulation, the engineered biointerfaces generate physiologically relevant electrical potentials while maintaining radical-scavenging activity without inducing reactive oxygen species. The localized bioelectrical communication due to their desired cell-adhesiveness activates calcium signaling, cytoskeletal reorganization, extracellular matrix remodeling, and immunomodulatory programs, leading to enhanced cell migration in vitro and coordinated axonal regeneration, remyelination, angiogenesis, and functional recovery after spinal cord injury in rats. Generally, a general molecular design principle is established linking peptide sequence, hierarchical assembly, and biointerface function, demonstrating that electromechanical conversion and biological communication can be coprogrammed within biodegradable supramolecular materials for neural regeneration.

title: Dual‐Force Strategy for Universal Clusteroluminescence in Non‐Conjugated Small Molecules
abstract: ABSTRACT Non‐traditional luminophores (NTLs) without extended π‐conjugation are attractive for bio‐applications, yet an effective strategy to impart bright emission to non‐luminescent small molecules remains challenging. In this work, we report a modular strategy based on the diethylenetriamine (DETA)‐induced universal luminescence (DIUL) effect, which converts simple non‐conjugated precursors into highly emissive cluster‐based small molecules via synergistic dual‐force: ionic (─BF 4 − /─NH 2 + ) and hydrogen‐bonding (─NH─/─NH 2 ) interactions. The resulting seven derivatives exhibit >70% photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) in water, with emission independent of ring/chain structure, demonstrating a robust dual‐force mechanism that advances beyond hydrogen‐bond‐dominated aggregation‐induced emission (AIE) models. These probes show excellent water solubility, low cytotoxicity, and efficient cellular uptake, enabling high‐contrast dual‐color cellular and deep 3D tumor spheroid imaging, along with long‐term biocompatible zebrafish imaging. This work establishes a versatile modular functionalization platform for bright NTLs, offering fundamental insights into cooperative non‐covalent interactions and opening new avenues for designing multifunctional optical materials in bioimaging, sensing, and encryption.

title: Coupling Iodine Regulation With Hole‐Selective Interfaces for Efficient and Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Operational instability remains a major barrier to the practical application of perovskite solar cells (PSCs), where the formation and volatilization of molecular iodine (I 2 ) cause irreversible degradation of both the perovskite and adjacent hole‐transport layer (HTL). Existing iodine‐trapping or reducing agents can mitigate this degradation, but often compromise interfacial charge transport. Here, we develop two amidinium‐based interfacial modifiers, PTZ‐PEFAI and PXZ‐PEFAI, that combine iodine regulation, favorable energy‐level alignment, and defect passivation. Density functional theory calculations and experiments show that the S/O sites of phenothiazine (PTZ) and phenoxazine (PXZ) interact with I 2 through halogen bonding, enabling I 2 capture and dissociation. The direct identification of I 3 − in modifier‐iodine cocrystals further supports the regeneration of iodide ions. At the perovskite surface, these interactions suppress iodine loss, replenish iodide, and promote healing of iodine‐vacancy defects. Meanwhile, the p‐type PTZ/PXZ functionalities improve energy‐level alignment and facilitate hole extraction at the perovskite/HTL interface. Consequently, PTZ‐PEFAI‐treated n–i–p PSCs achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.34% and a T 85 lifetime exceeding 1500 h under maximum‐power‐point tracking at 65°C. This work provides a molecular design strategy for simultaneously regulating interfacial iodine chemistry and charge transport toward efficient and stable PSCs.

title: Heat‐Activated Reversible Conjugation Switching in Polymers Through Cooperative Ion Pairing
abstract: ABSTRACT Thermochromic conjugated polymers generally undergo transitions from colored to less‐colored states upon heating due to disruption of π‐conjugation. In contrast, heat‐triggered switching from a colorless state to a more intensely colored conjugated state remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a reversible conjugation‐switching polymer system governed by cooperative interactions between metal cations and counteranions. By incorporating lactone‐functionalized xanthene units directly into conjugated polymer backbones, weakly solvated Li + , Na + , and Ag + ions, acting cooperatively with their weakly coordinating counteranions, induce lactone ring opening and establish linear conjugation along the polymer backbone, thereby producing pronounced optical responses. Coordination of the metal ions by isopropanol reverses the process and restores the colorless state. A series of conjugated copolymers displayed thermally activated multicolor responses spanning blue, green, yellow, orange, red, magenta, and black, enabling rewritable invisible‐ink systems on paper substrates. Density functional theory calculations support a nearly barrierless Li + /PF 6 − ion‐pair‐cooperation‐promoted ring‐opening process and reveal reversible switching between twisted nonconjugated and planar linearly conjugated states. These results establish a metal‐ion‐regulated conjugation‐switching strategy for heat‐activated colorless‐to‐colored switching and responsive optical materials.

title: Single‐Atom Multi‐Hydrogen Adsorption Enables Ultrafast Charge Transfer for Boosting Photocatalytic H 2 Production
abstract: ABSTRACT Single‐atom cocatalysts with near‐100% atom utilization are widely studied for boosting photocatalytic H 2 evolution, but their mechanistic insights remain largely restricted to idealized mono‐hydrogen adsorption models. Such simplified frameworks fail to capture the complexity of operando reaction environments, where the high coordination unsaturation of single atoms inevitably drives a transition toward multi‐hydrogen adsorption states. Here, we demonstrate that an N‐coordinated Ni single‐atom cocatalyst (Ni SA ‐N) forms a multi‐hydrogen adsorption state during actual photocatalytic H 2 evolution, significantly accelerating ultrafast charge transfer kinetics. Research results demonstrate that the adsorption of multiple hydrogen triggers spontaneous free‐electron delocalization, rendering the Ni center into a unique electron‐deficient (δ + ) feature. This dynamic electronic reconfiguration enhances the interfacial d‐p orbital hybridization between Ni SA and S of CdS, effectively shortening the interfacial Ni–S bond to construct a highly conductive channel that facilitates ultrafast electron transfer from the CdS to Ni SA cocatalyst, as elucidated by femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy. Consequently, the Ni SA ‐N/CdS system achieves an exceptional H 2 evolution rate of 20.20 mmol h −1 g −1 . This work identifies the multi‐hydrogen adsorption state as a pivotal nexus linking surface chemistry to ultrafast dynamics, providing a conceptual framework for engineering high‐performance catalysts for artificial photosynthesis.

title: Globally antiaromatic anthracene–porphyrin nanobelts
abstract: Abstract Conjugated molecular belts attract increasing attention because of the unusual electronic and magnetic behaviour arising from their radially oriented p orbitals. A π-conjugated molecular belt is expected to behave like a quantum ring, showing global aromatic or antiaromatic ring currents, but in most hydrocarbon benzenoid belts, localized Clar sextets preclude the emergence of global ring currents. Here we report the synthesis of anthracene-bridged porphyrin nanobelts that sustain global antiaromatic ring currents in the neutral state. Macrocyclization was achieved by nickel(0)-mediated Yamamoto coupling. Scholl oxidation with DDQ/TfOH, promoted by electron-donating methoxy substituents, yielded the strained triple-stranded nanobelts. These hybrid nanobelts show global antiaromaticity, with Hückel circuits of 72, 96 or 120 π electrons, as revealed by 1 H NMR spectroscopy and corroborated by computational analysis. This work establishes a platform for synthesizing other heterocyclic nanobelts, in cases where the corresponding hydrocarbon nanobelt is not yet synthetically accessible.

title: Rational Design of a Chiral Hybrid Ge(II) Halide With Giant Chiroptical Activity for Circularly Polarized Light Detection
abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral hybrid metal halides integrate semiconducting optoelectronic functionality with intrinsic chirality, offering new opportunities in the field of next‐generation chiral photonics and spintronics. However, the incorporation of chiral organic ligands alone is often insufficient to induce pronounced chiral structural distortions, thereby limiting the resulting chiroptical activity. Herein, we demonstrate for the first time that the stereochemically active 4s 2 lone‐pair of Ge 2+ can serve as an internal structural amplifier of chirality. We rationally designed and synthesized a pair of enantiomeric chiral hybrid Ge(II) halides, denoted as ( R / S ‐MBA)GeI 3 (MBA is methylbenzylammonium). Specifically, the strong lone‐pair expression in ( R / S ‐MBA)GeI 3 drives significant chirality‐favorable distortions, manifested by a large asymmetric bond angle variance and projected deflection angle of the chiral [−Ge−I−] ∞ chains. This enhanced structural chirality increases the circular dichroism (CD) anisotropy factor ( g CD ) of ( R / S ‐MBA)GeI 3 to 2.66 times that of the Pb(II) homologs. Benefiting from the superior chiroptical activity, ( R / S ‐MBA)GeI 3 further exhibits second‐harmonic generation (SHG)‐CD anisotropy factor ( g SHG‐CD ) values of −1.17/1.09, while the corresponding devices achieve photocurrent anisotropy factors ( g Iph ) of −0.403/0.391. Finally, we demonstrated a proof‐of‐concept circularly polarized light‐encrypted optical communication system. Our work provides a new insight into the rational design of high‐performance chiral functional materials.

title: Desmin filaments extend along actin filaments within the mouse skeletal muscle sarcomere
abstract: Abstract Although desmin intermediate filaments are critical for muscle architecture and homeostasis, their spatial 3D organization remains elusive. Their known localization to sarcomeric Z-lines delimits the periodic array of actin and myosin filaments. Here, using d STORM and SIM sub-diffraction resolution microscopy, we resolve the spatial 3D organization of desmin filaments within mouse skeletal muscle, and reveal they are not confined to Z-lines. Our reconstruction reveals that desmin intermediate filaments extend from Z-lines into the sarcomere interior, where they align with actin filaments. Functional assays show that disrupting desmin filament assembly in normal male mouse muscle using a dominant negative inhibitor of desmin selectively reduces active tension at longer sarcomere lengths, indicating a role for desmin in sarcomere mechanics. These findings expand the structural model of the muscle sarcomere and support a role for desmin in force production.

title: Interfacial Engineering of Triboelectric-Enhanced MXene/Covalent Organic Framework Heterostructures for Rapid Sensing of Trace NH3 with Real-Time Visualization
abstract: Abstract Self-powered ammonia (NH3) sensing has emerged as a promising strategy for environmental monitoring and industrial safety owing to its capability of eliminating external power supplies. However, due to the insufficient number of active sites and slow gas diffusion kinetics in traditional sensing materials, achieving both high sensitivity and fast response to low concentrations of NH3 remains a major challenge. Herein, an MXCOF-5 heterostructure was constructed through in situ growth of a boronate ester-linked covalent organic framework (COF-5) on Ti3C2Tx MXene and subsequently integrated into an electrospun polyacrylonitrile nanofiber membrane. The π–π conjugated network of COF-5 and the polar functional groups on the Ti3C2Tx MXene surface synergistically facilitate charge separation and transport, providing abundant active sites and ordered nanochannels. Meanwhile, the Lewis acid active sites and surface defects of the material enable selective NH3 adsorption. The triboelectric nanogenerator (MCP-TENG) achieved a high output voltage of 314.6 V and a current of 20.1 μA. The triboelectric nanosensor (MCP-TENS) achieved highly sensitive and selective NH3 detection with a limit of detection as low as 0.75 ppm and rapid response/recovery times of 7/11 s. Furthermore, the MCP-TENS was integrated into a wireless NH3 detection platform, enabling real-time on-site visualization of NH3 concentrations. This work opens broad prospects for self-powered gas sensing systems toward distributed environmental monitoring.

title: Self-Assembled Naphthalocyanine Molecular Lattices as a Platform for Tunable Quantum Superlattices
abstract: Compared to van der Waals moiré systems, molecular assembly offers an alternative platform for superlattice engineering via heterointegration. The electronic properties of the self-assembled square-lattice monolayer of metal-free naphthalocyanine (H2Nc), in particular its band dispersion and tunability by metal substrates, remain less explored. Using density functional theory, we compare the electronic structure of a free-standing H2Nc monolayer with that of H2Nc lattices assembled on noble metal substrates. In the free-standing film, we identify nearly flat, molecule-localized states and more dispersive bands, each compactly described by an anisotropic tight-binding Hamiltonian yielding band-resolved hopping anisotropies. We further show theoretically the wide tunability of intersite hopping and Coulomb interaction through the dielectric and screening environment. On Ag(100), orbital hybridization between molecular frontier states and the substrate drives finite spectral weight at the Fermi level and local interfacial polarization, enhancing the effective intermolecular hopping roughly thirty-fold and drastically reducing U/t. Experimentally, angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy resolves substantial interfacial charge redistribution and an enhanced bandwidth of the highest occupied molecular orbital, with the substrate coupling stronger on Ag(100) than Au(111), consistent with theory. Although static calculations exhibit an intrinsic C2 hopping anisotropy set by the two central hydrogens, thermal averaging over tautomer configurations at 77 K restores an effectively C4-symmetric dispersion while preserving the bandwidth. These results clarify how metal substrates and gates convert H2Nc from isolated molecules into a tunable 2D lattice, and highlight molecular superlattices as a platform in which effective interaction parameters can be widely engineered.

title: Multifunctional Organic Ammonium Salt for Synergistic Crystallization and Defect Regulation in Wide‐Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskites with low defect density and high crystallization quality are essential for high‐performance tandem solar cells. Here, we introduce a multifunctional organic ammonium salt, DFPACl, into a 1.67 eV WBG perovskite precursor to simultaneously regulate crystallization dynamics and suppress defect formation. The ammonium functional group in DFPACl strongly interacts with undercoordinated halide/Pb ions and synergistically couples with the [PbX 6 ] 4− octahedral framework, endowing the additive with dual functionalities of inhibiting detrimental defect generation and promoting ordered crystal growth in WBG perovskite films. As a result, the DFPACl‐doped films exhibit reduced trap densities, optimized energy‐level alignment, and enhanced charge extraction capability. Consequently, the corresponding solar cells achieve a significantly improved open‐circuit voltage from 1.210 to 1.255 V, along with an enhanced power conversion efficiency from 21.51% to 23.08%. Moreover, the unencapsulated devices demonstrate the superior long‐term stability. This work provides a simple yet effective additive‐engineering strategy for developing efficient and stable WBG perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Electric-field-assisted interfacial rubrene self-assembly for continuous tuning of liquid crystal pretilt angles
abstract: Abstract This study demonstrates a contact-free, low-temperature strategy for continuously tuning the pretilt angle of nematic liquid crystals (LCs) via electric-field-assisted capillary filling combined with rubrene self-assembly. By applying an AC electric field (0–5 V) across unrubbed, polyimide-free indium tin oxide cells during LC injection, the pretilt angle of a rubrene-doped nematic LC mixture can be continuously programmed from approximately 3° (near-planar) to 90° (homeotropic). Contact-angle analysis reveals that increasing the filling voltage dramatically alters the interfacial interaction from a polar-dominated surface to a nonpolar, high-dispersive regime, resulting in a gradual transition from planar to homeotropic LC alignment. Electro-optical and dielectric measurements confirm stable, uniform LC alignment and customized threshold responses across cycles. This field-imprinted interfacial assembly method eliminates mechanical damage and high-temperature thermal processing, offering a scalable route for next-generation flexible, wearable, and tunable photonic devices.

title: One-Step Fabrication of Amphiphilic Block Copolymer-Encapsulated Eu(III) Complex Aqueous Scintillator for Acid-Resistant X-ray Imaging
abstract: Abstract The development of lanthanide(III)-based aqueous scintillator for X-ray imaging has attracted considerable attention, however, the intrinsic hydrophobicity of these complexes severely limits their dispersibility in water. Herein, we propose a one-step strategy for the efficient preparation of block copolymer-encapsulated Eu(III) complex (Eu(III)@BCP) hybrid nanomaterials via ring-opening metathesis polymerization (ROMP) in a CH2Cl2/H2O emulsion. In this approach, two norbornenyl monomers (one bearing a hydrophilic tertiary amino and the other a hydrophobic benzyl group) along with a Eu(III) complex are dissolved in CH2Cl2/H2O emulsion. Upon injection of the Grubbs catalyst to initiate ROMP, the amphiphilic BCP with a well-defined structure is synthesized at the emulsion interface, concurrently encapsulating the Eu(III) complex and in situ forming latex particles. The water-dispersible Eu(III)@BCP hybrid nanomaterials are obtained via emulsion-induced self-assembly by volatilizing the CH2Cl2 phase. The Eu(III)@BCP hybrids exhibit excellent photoluminescence stability across a broad pH range (1–7) and are employed as aqueous scintillators for acid-resistant X-ray imaging. Overall, this work offers a straightforward polymer encapsulation route to aqueous scintillators suitable for X-ray imaging under highly acidic conditions.

title: Urea-carbon nanotube composites: Synthesis, characterization, and differential antibacterial activity against S. aureus and E. coli
abstract: This study focuses on the synthesis, characterization, and antibacterial assessment of urea-functionalized carbon nanotube (CNT) composites. Amide nanotubes can be formed through the self-assembly of amphiphilic molecules driven by hydrogen-bonding interactions; however, previously reported approaches may be limited by aggregation and difficulties in large-scale production. In the present work, CNTs were functionalized with urea and systematically characterized using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), thermogravimetric analysis, scanning electron microscopy, atomic force microscopy, and measurement of the zeta potential to evaluate their structural, chemical, thermal, morphological, and surface-charge properties. The results demonstrated the incorporation of urea-derived functionalities onto the CNT surface. Although functionalization decreased the thermal stability of the CNTs, the spectroscopic results indicated the presence of amide-related functional groups in the CNT–urea–CNT composite. Among the characterization techniques, XPS provided direct evidence of urea incorporation through the appearance of the N 1s signal and corresponding changes in the C 1s and O 1s spectra. Collectively, these results demonstrate substantial modification of the CNT surface following treatment with urea, without implying definitive covalent attachment. Measurement of the zeta potential further revealed a substantial alteration in the surface-charge behavior following functionalization. As pH increased, the zeta potential progressively decreased, a phenomenon that can be attributed to the deprotonation of surface functional groups. Pristine CNTs exhibited an isoelectric point (IEP) at approximately pH 7–8, whereas urea functionalization shifted the IEP to around pH 4, indicating a significant modification of the CNT surface chemistry. The urea–CNT and CNT–urea–CNT composites exhibited concentration-dependent antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli at 0.01–0.1 mg mL–1. The CNT–urea–CNT composite was more active against S. aureus at 0.05 and 0.1 mg mL–1, while the urea–CNT composite showed greater activity at 0.01 mg mL–1. The CNT–urea–CNT composite consistently exhibited stronger activity against E. coli, with a maximum inhibition zone of 33 ± 3.01 mm at 0.1 mg mL–1. These differences may reflect variations in surface structure, dispersion, and interactions with bacterial membranes.

title: Hyperconjugation‐Mediated Design of Dissolution‐Resistant Organic Cathode for Durable Zinc‐Ion Batteries
abstract: Small‐molecule organic carbonyl compounds (SMOCCs) have emerged as promising cathode candidates for aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) by virtue of their high theoretical capacity and tunable redox potential. However, their practical implementation is severely impeded by intrinsically poor electronic conductivity and pronounced dissolution in aqueous electrolytes, leading to unsatisfactory rate capability and cyclic stability. Herein, we report a hyper‐conjugative structural design strategy to construct a TAPT@rGO composite, in which 2,3,5,6‐tetraamino‐1,4‐benzoquinone (TABQ) and 1,10‐phenanthroline‐5，6‐dione (PTD) are covalently integrated with graphene oxide (GO) to yield a nitrogen‐heteroatom‐extended conjugated framework. This architecture not only ensures homogeneous dispersion of nanosized TAPT crystallites on the rGO substrate, but also establishes an N‐heterocycle‐mediated extended conjugation linkage between the organic species and the carbon scaffold, which synergistically enhances electronic transport kinetics and suppresses active material dissolution. As a cathode for AZIBs, the TAPT@rGO composite delivers a high initial capacity of 271 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 with an average operating voltage of 0.8 V, together with exceptional cycling stability (93.5% capacity retention over 100 cycles at 0.1 A g −1 and 82.5% retention over 10000 cycles at 5 A g −1 ). This work demonstrates that hyperconjugation engineering provides a rational molecular design for developing high‐performance organic cathodes toward durable multivalent ion storage.

title: Hierarchically Bridged Graphite Foam/Cellulose Aerogel Phase Change Composites Reconciling High Thermal Conductivity and Latent Heat
abstract: ABSTRACT Phase change composites (PCCs) are promising for thermal management and solar thermal storage, yet reconciling high thermal conductivity with high latent heat remains challenging. Thermally conductive scaffolds accelerate heat transfer but dilute the phase‐change component and disturb crystallization, whereas polymeric porous supports provide structural confinement but suffer from sluggish thermal transport. Herein, a hierarchical composite is constructed by forming a crosslinked hydroxyethyl cellulose‐polyethylene glycol (PEG) network within mesophase pitch‐based graphite foam (MPGF), followed by vacuum impregnation of the scaffold with PEG. The continuous MPGF provides a primary heat transfer pathway and mechanical reinforcement, while the directional cellulose network bridges and subdivides MPGF macropores into a secondary porous scaffold. The PEG segments in the cellulose network not only improve interfacial compatibility with the impregnated PEG but also guide its crystallization within the refined pores. Therefore, the composite exhibits a thermal conductivity of 53.41 W m −1 K −1 and a latent enthalpy of 196.83 J g −1 . Benefiting from rapid heat spreading and sustained thermal release, it achieves efficient solar‐thermal storage and delivers a thermoelectric voltage of 391.5 mV at 200 mW cm −2 . This hierarchical architecture offers an effective strategy for integrating rapid heat transfer, efficient latent‐heat utilization, and solar thermoelectric conversion in PCCs.
